Surplus B-17 bombers at the Kingman Army Air Base boneyard waiting to either be scrapped or sold after WW2. Arizona. c. 1946

The Kingman Army Airfield was built as a World War II United States Army Air Forces training field. Between 1942 and 1945 the U.S. Army Air Forces acquired about 4,145 acres in Mohave County outside of Kingman, Arizona.

After WW2, War Assets Administration came to Kingman AAF to set up Sales & Storage Depot No. 41. Approximately 5,500 warbirds were flown to Kingman in 1945 and 1946 for storage and sale. That number included several B-32 bombers that were flown there straight from the assembly line.

Most of the transports and trainers could be used in the civil fleet, and trainers were sold for $875 to $2,400. The fighters and bombers were of little peacetime use, although several P-38 Lightnings were sold to individuals for use in air racing and some bombers were transferred to schools and communities for memorial purposes. The rest were sold for scrap and the B-17 commanded the price of $13,750.

After Sales-Storage Depot No. 41 completed its job in late 1948, the airfield was turned over to Mohave County to be used as an airport for the county.
